courseTitle: How IT Teams Work: Agile, Waterfall, Scrum, Kanban & Software Releases

slots.practicalActivity: Pick a small project idea of your own (e.g. 'add a new report to a dashboard'), and write out how it would move through Waterfall's five phases versus Agile's sprint cycle; then write 3 user stories for it in the 'As a [role], I want [capability], so that [benefit]' shape, each with at least 2 checkable acceptance criteria; finally sketch a 5-column Kanban board (Backlog, To Do, In Progress, Review, Done) on paper or in a spreadsheet and place your 3 stories into it, moving one into To Do.
slots.deliverable: A written Waterfall-vs-Agile comparison for your chosen project, 3 user stories with acceptance criteria, and a populated 5-column Kanban board with those stories placed in it.

slots.practicalActivity: Walk one of your Kanban cards from the previous slot through the Dev -> QA -> UAT -> Prod chain, writing one sentence per environment describing what question it answers and who owns it; then, using Git, create a new local repository, make a commit, create a branch, make a second commit on that branch, and write a short pull-request description for merging it back; finally diagram which CI/CD stage (build, automated test, deploy to staging, deploy to production) your card's change would need to pass, and write one rollback-plan sentence for it.
slots.deliverable: A written Dev/QA/UAT/Prod walkthrough for one card, a real local Git repository with at least 2 commits across 2 branches and a pull-request description, and a one-sentence rollback plan for the change.

slots.practicalActivity: Watch the Castlebridge Retail capstone scenario: a sales director's emailed request for a dashboard showing revenue by region and by product category, refreshed automatically. Read the full checklist it sets up for the hands-on lab that follows: user stories, a Kanban board, a build/test plan, a UAT sign-off, release notes, and a production incident.
slots.deliverable: Written notes breaking the sales director's one-paragraph request into its distinct pieces (the region view, the category view, the automatic refresh), ready to turn into user stories in the lab that follows.

slots.practicalActivity: Complete the Castlebridge Retail capstone: write user stories (with acceptance criteria) for the revenue-by-region view, the revenue-by-category view, and the automatic daily refresh; build a Kanban board and move your stories through its columns; write a short QA test plan for each story including at least one edge case (e.g. a region with zero sales for the month); write a one-paragraph UAT sign-off in the sales director's voice, either approving the work or sending back specific feedback; write short, specific release notes for the launch; and write up how you'd investigate and communicate about a simulated production incident where last month's numbers show zero for one region two days after launch.
slots.deliverable: A complete written capstone packet: 3 user stories with acceptance criteria, a Kanban board showing their progress through its columns, a QA test plan per story, a UAT sign-off, release notes, and a production-incident response writeup.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course, a student understands how real IT departments plan, track, test, approve, and release work -- Agile/Waterfall, Scrum roles and sprints, Kanban boards, the Dev/QA/UAT/Prod chain, Git, and CI/CD -- and has practiced it end-to-end on a simulated business request.
